result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers open by calling the spec solid, then pile on a long list of new requirements: A has seven sections, and B has eight items plus four extras. That goes against the rubric's call for one or two small suggestions and a short answer. Both also re-open things the spec already covers, such as status states, the off switch and undo. A adds suggest-only mode and holding changes for review, which move toward a review workflow. B adds operational extras (metrics, paging, privacy, time zones) and a shadow mode, so neither is clearly better. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers open by calling the spec solid and credit the scope limit, abstain behaviour and undo, but neither credits the visible status line. Both then pile on long lists of new requirements. B goes further toward heavier workflow, with batch-accept suggest-only mode, holding big runs as suggestions, and a rules-management page. B is also slightly longer, so A edges it on restraint.
